entry: Middle High German epic poem from around 1200, written by an anonymous poet probably from the Passau region. It draws on oral Germanic heroic legend. The first part tells how the hero Siegfried seeks the hand of the Burgundian princess Kriemhild and is murdered by the vassal Hagen. The second part recounts Kriemhild's revenge through her marriage to Etzel, king of the [[Huns]], which ends in the destruction of the Burgundians and of Etzel's kingdom. It was the first heroic epic written down in the German vernacular. A sequel, the *Nibelungenklage*, was composed soon afterward to soften its tragedy. Forgotten after about 1500, it was rediscovered in 1755 and became a German national epic, though Nazi propaganda later exploited it. Its best-known legacy is [[Richard Wagner]]'s operatic cycle *Der Ring des Nibelungen*, which draws mostly on Old Norse sources. In 2009 its three main manuscripts were inscribed in UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.

French inventor and pioneer of photography. Niépce developed heliography, a technique that produced the world's oldest surviving products of a photographic process. In the mid-1820s he used a primitive camera to make the oldest surviving photograph of a real-world scene. Inspired by the [[Camera obscura|camera obscura]], he sought a way to fix its images permanently. Niépce served as a staff officer in the French army under [[Napoleon]] before turning to scientific research. With his older brother Claude, he conceived and developed the Pyréolophore, one of the world's first [[Internal combustion engine|internal combustion engines]]. Financially ruined, he died of a stroke, and his grave was financed by the municipality.

Country in Central America (pop., 2026: 7,097,329), the largest in the region by area. [[Managua]] is the capital and largest city. The [[Spanish Empire]] conquered the region in the 16th century, and Nicaragua gained independence from [[Spain]] in 1821. The Caribbean region of Mosquitia was an independent kingdom under British protection until 1860, when the Treaty of Managua brought it into union with Nicaragua. Since independence the country has experienced [[Dictatorship|dictatorship]], American occupation, a revolution and the Contra War. Under Daniel Ortega, president since 2007, democratic backsliding led to a crackdown after large protests in 2018, and after the 2021 election the country was widely described as an authoritarian dictatorship. Nicaragua is known for its fertile soil and for the Bosawás Biosphere Reserve, the second-largest [[Rainforest|tropical rainforest]] of the Americas. It is a founding member of the [[United Nations]].

Italian violinist, guitarist and composer. Regarded as the most celebrated violin virtuoso of his time, Paganini was one of the pillars of modern violin technique. His 24 Caprices for Solo Violin, Op. 1 are among his best-known compositions. The son of a ship chandler from Genoa, he studied with Alessandro Rolla, Ferdinando Paer and Gasparo Ghiretti. In 1805 he entered the service of [[Napoleon]]'s sister, Elisa Bonaparte, at Lucca. From 1809 he toured Europe, building a reputation for technical brilliance and showmanship. He ended his concert career in 1834 amid declining health, and the failure of a Paris casino left him in financial ruin. He died in [[Nice]], then part of the Kingdom of Sardinia. His influence on composers such as [[Franz Liszt]] was considerable.

City and port on the French Riviera (pop., 2025: 353,701), prefecture of the Alpes-Maritimes department in southeastern France. Nice lies on the Mediterranean at the foot of the French Alps and was the capital of the historical County of Nice. The Terra Amata site contains evidence of early use of fire about 380,000 years ago. Greeks from Marseille founded a settlement called Nikaia around 350 BC. The town was a dominion of Savoy from 1388 and was annexed by France in 1860. In the 18th century aristocratic families began wintering there, and the Promenade des Anglais, inaugurated in 1931, is named for these visitors. Painters including [[Henri Matisse]] and [[Marc Chagall]] were drawn to its light, and [[Friedrich Nietzsche]] wrote *Thus Spoke Zarathustra* there. UNESCO designated Nice a World Heritage Site in 2021.

Statement of Christian belief adopted at the [[First Council of Nicaea]] in 325. It affirms that Jesus is divine and "begotten of the Father", a position opposed to [[Arianism]]. According to the traditional view, the First Council of Constantinople amended the creed in 381, and the amended version is known as the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed. It forms part of the profession of faith in the [[Eastern Orthodox Church]], the [[Catholic Church]], Lutheran, Anglican and many Protestant traditions. In liturgical churches it is usually recited on Sundays and major festivals.

American actress, singer and dancer, best known for playing Lieutenant Uhura in *Star Trek* and its film sequels. Her portrayal was groundbreaking for African American actresses on American television. Nichols began her career as a singer and dancer, touring with the bands of [[Duke Ellington]] and Lionel Hampton, and she appeared as the principal dancer in the 1959 film *Porgy and Bess*. From 1977 to 2015 she volunteered to promote [[NASA]]'s programs and recruit diverse astronauts, including some of the first female and ethnic minority astronauts.

Last Emperor of Russia (r. 1894–1917), a member of the Romanov dynasty. Nicholas II oversaw the Russian Empire's role in the [[Russo-Japanese War]] and in [[World War I]]. Although he ostensibly presided over a constitutional monarchy after the Duma was established, he resisted political reform and retained autocratic control. Defeat in the Russo-Japanese War and the 1905 revolution weakened his standing, and military losses and economic hardship in World War I eroded public confidence in his rule. He abdicated in March 1917 during the February Revolution, ending 304 years of Romanov rule. He and his family were imprisoned and later executed by the [[Bolsheviks]] at [[Yekaterinburg]] during the [[Russian Civil War]]. Most historians regard him as a well-intentioned but poor ruler. The [[Russian Orthodox Church]] canonized him and his family as passion-bearers in 2000.

Emperor of Russia, king of Poland and grand duke of [[Finland]] (r. 1825–1855). His reign began with the failed Decembrist revolt and is remembered as reactionary and repressive. It saw territorial expansion, including territory seized from Qajar Iran in the Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828 and the resumed conquest of the [[Caucasus]]. He crushed the November Uprising in Poland in 1831 and aided Austria during the Hungarian Revolution of 1848. His reign ended in the [[Crimean War]] (1853–1856), which went disastrously for Russia. Several historians have concluded that his reign was "a catastrophic failure in both domestic and foreign policy". At his death the [[Russian Empire]] spanned over 20 million square kilometers, but it was in urgent need of reform.

British stockbroker and humanitarian. Nicholas Winton helped rescue 669 children, mostly Jewish, from [[Czechoslovakia]] on the eve of the Second World War. The operation became known as the Czech Kindertransport. In Britain he arranged the legal requirements for the children's entry and found them homes and sponsors. His role remained largely unknown for nearly 50 years, until he appeared on the BBC program *That's Life!* in 1988 and was reunited with children he had helped. He was knighted in 2003 for services to humanity, and in 2014 the Czech Republic awarded him the Order of the White Lion.

British singer-songwriter and guitarist. Drake signed to Island Records while still a student at the [[University of Cambridge]] and released three albums: *Five Leaves Left* (1969), *Bryter Layter* (1971) and *Pink Moon* (1972). He did not reach a wide audience during his lifetime. Suffering from depression, he withdrew from performing and recording after *Pink Moon* and died of an overdose of antidepressants at his parents' home in Warwickshire. His music was reassessed after the 1979 release of the retrospective collection *Fruit Tree*, and he has influenced many later artists.

American football coach and sportscaster. Saban coached Michigan State, Louisiana State University and the University of Alabama, and he served as head coach of the Miami Dolphins of the [[National Football League]]. At Alabama, from 2007 to 2023, his teams won six claimed national championships and one unclaimed title. Across his college career he won seven claimed national titles, the most in college football history. He was the first coach to win a national championship with two different Football Bowl Subdivision schools. Saban later became an analyst for [[ESPN]]'s College GameDay.

Silvery-white transition metal, chemical element with symbol Ni and atomic number 28. Nickel is hard, ductile and resistant to corrosion, because a thin layer of nickel oxide forms on its surface. It is one of only four elements that are [[Ferromagnetism|ferromagnetic]] at about room temperature. Axel Fredrik Cronstedt first isolated and classified the element in 1751, initially mistaking its ore for a copper mineral. Its name comes from a mischievous sprite of German miner folklore. Economically important ores are sulfides, especially pentlandite. About 68% of world production is used in [[Stainless steel|stainless steel]], and further amounts go into alloys, plating, [[Coin|coins]] and rechargeable batteries, including those in electric vehicles.

American children's pay television channel, launched on April 1, 1979, as the first cable channel for children. Its name comes from early five-cent movie theaters called nickelodeons. The channel began as a test broadcast in December 1977 on QUBE, an interactive cable system in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. It was commercial-free until advertising was introduced in January 1984. Its sister channels include Nick Jr. and Nicktoons, and its best-known shows include *[[SpongeBob SquarePants]]*. As of December 2023 it was available in about 70 million pay television households in the United States, down from a peak of 101 million in 2011.

Trinidadian rapper and singer-songwriter, regarded as the "Queen of Rap" and as one of the most influential rappers of all time. Raised in New York City, she gained recognition with mixtapes before her debut studio album, *Pink Friday* (2010), topped the US Billboard 200. Her 2023 album *Pink Friday 2* gave her three US number-one albums, the most of any female rapper. She has sold over 100 million records, and in 2023 Billboard and Vibe ranked her the greatest female rapper of all time. She has also acted, voiced animated films, and served as a judge on [[American Idol]] in 2013.

Venezuelan politician and former union leader who served as president of [[Venezuela]] from 2013 to 2026. He was foreign minister and vice president under [[Hugo Chávez]], and succeeded him on his death, winning the 2013 special election. Political analysts classified his government as a dictatorship from 2017, and he was accused of electoral fraud, censorship and human rights abuses. The [[United Nations]] and Human Rights Watch have alleged thousands of extrajudicial killings. In 2026 he was seized in a U.S. military raid and taken to the United States on drug trafficking charges, to which he pleaded not guilty.

Romanian communist leader and general secretary of the Romanian Communist Party from 1965 to 1989. He was also head of state from 1967 until 1989. Initially he eased press censorship and condemned the [[Warsaw Pact]] invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968, which gained him popularity. His regime soon became more repressive, and the Securitate secret police conducted mass surveillance. His population policies led to illegal [[Abortion|abortions]] and more orphans in state institutions. Austerity to repay foreign debt was effective but unpopular, and a [[Cult of personality|cult of personality]] grew around him. Protests in Timișoara in December 1989 led to the Romanian revolution. After Ceaușescu ordered the army to fire on demonstrators, he and his wife Elena were captured, tried and executed by firing squad.

American actor and film producer, born Nicolas Kim Coppola, known for his versatility across film genres. Cage won the Academy Award for Best Actor for *Leaving Las Vegas* (1995). He then became an action star in films such as *The Rock* (1996), *Con Air* (1997), *Face/Off* (1997) and the *National Treasure* series. After a period of straight-to-video productions, he gained renewed critical recognition for *Mandy* (2018), *Pig* (2021) and *Dream Scenario* (2023). He is the nephew of director [[Francis Ford Coppola]]. His production company, Saturn Films, has produced films including *Shadow of the Vampire* (2000).

French military engineer and physicist. A graduate of the École polytechnique, Carnot published his only work, *Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire* (1824), in which he developed the first successful theory of the maximum efficiency of heat engines. The essay attracted little notice during his lifetime, and he died in relative obscurity. In 1834 the French engineer Émile Clapeyron explained and extended it, and [[Lord Kelvin|William Thomson]] used Carnot's analysis to develop an absolute thermodynamic temperature scale. Rudolf Clausius used it to define [[Entropy|entropy]] and to formalize the [[Second law of thermodynamics|second law of thermodynamics]]. Carnot is often called the "father of thermodynamics".

French painter of the classical Baroque style, who worked mostly in [[Rome]]. Poussin trained in Paris around 1612 and went to Rome in 1624, where he studied [[Raphael]] and befriended artists who shared his classicizing tendencies. His paintings, mostly of religious and mythological subjects, are marked by clarity, logic and order, and they favor line over color. He returned to France in 1640 to serve as First Painter to [[Louis XIII]], but soon went back to Rome. In his later years he gave growing prominence to landscape, as in *The Seasons*. Until the 20th century he remained an inspiration for classically oriented artists, including [[Jacques-Louis David]], [[Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres|Ingres]] and [[Paul Cézanne|Cézanne]].

French politician who served as president of France from 2007 to 2012. He won the 2007 presidential election against the Socialist candidate Ségolène Royal. His term included the [[2008 financial crisis]], the [[Russo-Georgian War]], for which he negotiated a ceasefire, and the [[Arab Spring]]. He lost the 2012 election to François Hollande. He has been convicted in several cases, including corruption in 2021 and criminal conspiracy in 2025 over alleged Libyan financing of his 2007 campaign. He maintains his innocence and was released after about three weeks of a five-year sentence in 2025.

German engineer and inventor of the four-stroke [[Internal combustion engine|internal combustion engine]]. In 1864 Otto partnered with Eugen Langen to found N.A. Otto & Cie in [[Cologne]], which was the first company devoted entirely to designing and producing internal combustion engines. Their early free-piston engine was a commercial success but reached a technical dead end. Otto then turned to the four-stroke cycle, which he had failed to develop in 1862. The resulting Otto Silent Engine, not the Otto and Langen engine, is the basis of the "Otto cycle". A DIN standard defines an Otto engine as one in which the compressed fuel-air mixture is ignited by a timed spark.

Australian and American actress and producer, known for blockbusters and independent films. Kidman won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her role as Virginia Woolf in *The Hours* (2002). Her other films include *Dead Calm* (1989), *Moulin Rouge!* (2001) and *Eyes Wide Shut* (1999). She produced and starred in the HBO series *Big Little Lies*, for which she won Primetime Emmy Awards. She has been a goodwill ambassador for [[UNICEF]] since 1994. She has consistently ranked among the world's highest-paid actresses since the late 1990s.

Treatise on ethics by [[Aristotle]], in ten books. It asks how humans should live and identifies the good for human life as the goal at which all actions aim. Aristotle treats ethics as practical rather than theoretical, and he connects it to his [[Politics]]. The title may refer to Aristotle's son Nicomachus or to his father. The text appears to be lecture notes rather than a work Aristotle prepared for publication. In the Middle Ages it was one of the core works of philosophy, and [[Thomas Aquinas]] developed a synthesis of Aristotelian ethics with Christian theology. It remained the main authority on ethics at Protestant universities well into the 17th century, and it inspired the modern revival of [[Virtue|virtue]] ethics.

Capital of Cyprus and the last divided capital in Europe. Nicosia has been continuously inhabited for over 5,500 years. Its northern part is the de facto capital of [[Northern Cyprus]]. After intercommunal violence followed independence from Britain in 1960, the city's Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities segregated in 1964. Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974, days after a Greek junta-backed coup, and the dividing line ran through Nicosia. Apart from its government functions, the city is the island's financial capital and main international business center. It is the southeasternmost capital in the [[European Union]].
